result.stdout:
Analyze files or directories and list functions by complexity

Usage: dgf analyze [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or directories to analyze (.gitignore is respected)
          
          [default: .]

Options:
      --top <TOP>
          Rows to show in the table, 0 = all [default: 20, or `top` in dgf.toml]

      --coverage <PATH>
          Coverage report (Cobertura, OpenCover or LCOV) or folder with reports; adds CRAP scores (repeatable)

      --no-baseline
          Do not apply .dgf/baseline.json

      --save-history
          Also save a snapshot of this run for `dgf history`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Report format

          Possible values:
          - table:           Aligned columns for the terminal
          - json:            Everything, for other tools
          - markdown:        GitHub-flavored Markdown, for PR comments and job summaries
          - html:            A self-contained page with charts
          - sarif:           SARIF 2.1.0, for GitHub code scanning and editors
          - agent:           Compact text for AI assistants: only what needs attention
          - mutation-report: The mutation-testing-elements JSON report (`dgf mutate --run` only)
          
          [default: table]

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write the report to this file instead of the terminal

      --warn <N>
          Flag functions above this complexity [default: 10, or `warn` in dgf.toml]

      --fail <N>
          Exit with code 1 if a function is above this complexity [default: `fail` in dgf.toml]

      --exclude <PATTERN>
          Skip files or folders matching this .gitignore-style pattern (repeatable)

      --no-config
          Ignore dgf.toml

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Compare your branch and uncommitted edits with a base branch

Usage: dgf changes [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --base <REF>
          Branch or commit to compare with [default: `base` in dgf.toml, else main or master; HEAD with --staged]

      --staged
          Compare only what is staged for the next commit (used by the pre-commit hook)

      --scope <SCOPE>
          Which functions in changed files to report [default: lines]

          Possible values:
          - lines: Functions that contain a changed line
          - files: Every function in a changed file

      --fail-on <FAIL_ON>
          Which reported functions can fail the run [default: new-or-worse]

          Possible values:
          - new-or-worse: New functions and functions whose score went up
          - touched:      Every reported function, including ones whose score did not change

      --format <FORMAT>
          Report format

          Possible values:
          - table:           Aligned columns for the terminal
          - json:            Everything, for other tools
          - markdown:        GitHub-flavored Markdown, for PR comments and job summaries
          - html:            A self-contained page with charts
          - sarif:           SARIF 2.1.0, for GitHub code scanning and editors
          - agent:           Compact text for AI assistants: only what needs attention
          - mutation-report: The mutation-testing-elements JSON report (`dgf mutate --run` only)
          
          [default: table]

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write the report to this file instead of the terminal

      --warn <N>
          Flag functions above this complexity [default: 10, or `warn` in dgf.toml]

      --fail <N>

result.stdout:
Mutation testing: choose functions, list their mutants, or run them against the tests

Usage: dgf mutate [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or directories to mutate (not used with --changes)
          
          [default: .]

Options:
      --changes
          Only functions that this branch and its uncommitted edits changed

      --base <REF>
          Base for --changes [default: `base` in dgf.toml, else main or master]

      --min-complexity <N>
          Only functions with at least this cyclomatic complexity
          
          [default: 1]

      --show
          List every mutant, not only the count per function

      --run
          Build and test the mutants (C#, TypeScript, JavaScript): score per function, and every mutant no test noticed

      --jobs <N>
          Mutant test runs at the same time with --run [default: `jobs` in dgf.toml, else CPU cores - 1]

      --fail-under <PERCENT>
          With --run, exit with code 1 when the mutation score is below this percentage [default: `thresholds.break` in dgf.toml]

      --timeout-factor <N>
          A test run counts as hanging after (startup + its tests' time without mutants) × this [default: 1.5]

      --timeout-ms <MS>
          ... plus this many milliseconds [default: 5000]

      --build-jobs <N>
          Projects `dotnet build` builds at the same time (-m:N) [default: all cores]

      --low-priority
          Run dgf, its builds and its tests at below-normal priority

      --rerun-survivors
          With --run, test survivors again even when their code and tests did not change

      --cached
          With --run, report the cached results only and test nothing, such as to render another format of the last run; mutants without a cached result are listed as not in the cache

      --neighbours
          With --changes, also mutate the lines of other functions that hold a string key a changed function holds (such as "MemberPlanId"); their survivors are listed apart and left out of the score

      --no-mix
  
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Duplicated code that can be united: copies, near misses, reordered statements and, with --semantic, C# that does the same thing written differently and repeated queries (the same as `dgf-dup`)

Usage: dgf duplication [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          Files or folders to scan (honoring .gitignore)
          
          [default: .]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Possible values:
          - table: Readable text
          - agent: Compact text for AI assistants
          - json:  Everything, for other tools
          - html:  A self-contained page: the files with their copies, and each group
          
          [default: table]

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write the report to this file instead of the terminal

      --min-tokens <MIN_TOKENS>
          Fewest tokens a copy has
          
          [default: 50]

      --min-lines <MIN_LINES>
          Fewest lines a copy spans
          
          [default: 5]

      --tests
          Scan test code too

      --top <TOP>
          How many clone classes to show; 0 shows all
          
          [default: 20]

      --fail-above <PERCENT>
          Exit with code 1 when duplicated lines are above this share of all lines, in percent

      --changes
          Only findings with a copy in what this branch changed (since its merge base with --base, uncommitted and new files included); the whole repository is scanned, so copies of existing code are found

      --base <BASE>
          With --changes: the branch to compare with [default: main, else master]

      --fail-on-copies
          With --changes: exit with code 1 when the branch added any copy

      --semantic
          Also find C# methods that do the same thing written differently (a loop and its LINQ, `if` and `?:`), with the C# engine dgf-dup-cs

      --semantic-engine <PATH>
          The C# engine to run: an executable, or its .dll [default: DGF_DUP_CS, else dgf-dup-cs on PATH]

      --confirm
          With --semantic: run each group of methods said to do the same
[truncated]
